title: A more distant electric field
hook: Change distance from the charge and predict electric-field magnitude.
misconception: electric-field magnitude doubles when distance from the charge doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply E = kabs(q)/r² to compare electric-field magnitude when distance from the charge changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a fixed point charge in the same medium, E = kabs(q)/r². When distance from the charge doubles, electric-field magnitude becomes ¼ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model E = kabs(q)/r²; scaling exponent -2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a fixed point charge in the same medium, with a nonzero initial result. If distance from the charge triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on electric-field magnitude?
recall.why: Apply E = kabs(q)/r² under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/9.
